proposals.expected_failure_mode: Delay may still be weakly identified and compensate for misspecified generation time; can shift peaks rather than truly sharpen them, leading to split instability if timing differs across seasons.
proposals.rationale: Primary candidate matching the previous best spec. Fractional SEIRS can sharpen rise/fall while retaining parsimonious immunity-waning dynamics; a 2-week observation lag aligns with hospitalization timing without over-sweeping delay values, aiming for more stable peak timing across rolling splits.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Over-lagging can systematically delay peaks and broaden tails; may underpredict early surge and overpredict late-season persistence, especially if true lag is closer to 1–2 weeks.
proposals.rationale: Near-neighbor lag around the best region to test whether a slightly longer admissions lag improves peak alignment for high-peak, high-scale elderly series while keeping the same robust SEIRS fractional backbone.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Likely to lead peaks relative to observed hospitalizations (timing bias) and may require parameter compensation that distorts amplitude/width, especially in high-peak seasons.
proposals.rationale: Comparator without explicit observation lag to reduce non-identifiability and rolling-split variability. If fractional dynamics already capture rapid transients, direct I mapping may yield more stable timing than delayed_I when lag is not consistent across splits.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: H compartment may be weakly identifiable with limited weeks, causing over-parameterization and split instability; I+H can blur mechanistic meaning and may dampen sharp peaks or misattribute timing between I and H.
proposals.rationale: Single secondary comparator that modifies observation mapping to better reflect hospitalization-rate semantics without relying on an explicit fixed delay. Using I+H can act as a crude smoothing/lag proxy for admissions timing while avoiding a pure H-only mapping that may be too rigid in short series.
